'''Bernard Derrida''' ({{IPA|fr|dɛʁida|lang}}; born 1952) is a French [[Theoretical physics|theoretical]] [[physicist]]. He is best known for his work in [[statistical mechanics]], and is the eponym of ''Derrida plots'', an analytical technique for characterising differences between [[Boolean networks]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Evolution of overlaps between configurations in random Boolean networks|journal = Journal de Physique|date = 1986-08-01|pages = 1297–1303|volume = 47|issue = 8|doi = 10.1051/jphys:019860047080129700|first1 = B|last1 = Derrida|first2 = G|last2 = Weisbuch| url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/jpa-00210321/file/ajp-jphys_1986_47_8_1297_0.pdf }}</ref>

==Biography==
Derrida entered the [[École Normale Supérieure]] in 1971, and received his doctorate in 1976. Since 1993 he has been professor of physics at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|Université Pierre et Marie Curie]] and at ENS. He is an expert in statistical mechanics who has adapted statistical-physics ideas to various problems in biology.<ref>{{cite web | title=Bernard Derrida | url=http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/bernard-derrida | access-date=2011-02-05 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101228191714/http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/bernard-derrida# | archive-date=2010-12-28 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was elected, in 2004 to the [[Académie des sciences]].

In 2010, Derrida was awarded the [[Boltzmann Medal]] by [[IUPAP]] with [[John Cardy]].

In 2026, he was awarded the [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|ICTP Dirac Medal]] for his contributions to [[statistical mechanics]].<ref>[https://www.ictp.it/news/2026/8/ictp-announces-2026-dirac-medal-recipients Dirac Medallists 2026]</ref>

He is philosopher [[Jacques Derrida]]'s first cousin once removed<ref>Per https://carnetdujour.lefigaro.fr/annonce/print/6509428/ Bernard Derrida (1952–) is the son of Lucien Derrida (1916–2010); per https://gw.geneanet.org/adriel38?lang=fr&n=derrida&p=lucien the latter is the son of Jacob Derrida (1884–1966), himself son of Abraam Derrida (1853–1920), whereas per https://gw.geneanet.org/adriel38?lang=fr&n=derrida&p=jacques+elie Jacques Derrida (1930–2004) is the son of Haim Aimé Derrida (1896–1970), also son of Abraam Derrida.</ref>.
